_comment: Proposed answers for the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, project 11719. The BadgeApp reads this file and offers these values in the form; a maintainer still has to open the project and save. Only criteria that are true at this commit belong here. A value of '?' is ignored, so a placeholder is harmless. Format: docs/bestpractices-json.md in ossf/best-practices-badge.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/netresearch/timetracker/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md states eight security requirements and argues each one from the control that implements it, the test that fails if it stops holding, and what the argument leaves uncovered. It cites the threat model at https://github.com/netresearch/timetracker/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md, whose 'Trust boundaries' section identifies them and whose thirteen threats cover the common implementation weaknesses — LDAP injection, SQL injection, CSRF, XSS, privilege escalation in both directions, and hostile data from the Jira and Personio integrations — each with the control that answers it. The section 'Secure design principles, and where they show' argues deny by default, least privilege, complete mediation of half-finished logins and defence in depth from the configuration and code that implement them. A closing section names what the case does not argue: no second reviewer, Semgrep reports rather than blocks, and no fuzzing or penetration test.
